title: Potato Pie with Cold Meat
description: A pastry dish made with meat, tomatoes, and onion.
steps: Prepare some cold meat exactly as you did for the marrows, with the difference that you chop the tomatoes and onion with the meat
Season it well, and add to the mixture two extra eggs
Boil some floury potatoes according to the size you wish to make it
Cut them in pieces, put a little salt and very little water
When they are done drain them well
Mash them in the saucepan, taste and see if they are salted enough
If so, put some pepper, a little grated nutmeg, a little chopped parsley, 1 egg
Mash it all well together
Lay some at the bottom of your dish, grease it well first
Then put in the forced meat
Sprinkle the juice of half a lemon
Cover it over with the remainder of the mashed potatoes
Smooth it well, and crossbar it with a knife
Put in the oven to bake
Serve it in the same dish with another dish under

title: Potato Salad, No. 1
description: A salad made with potatoes, onion, and mustard.
steps: Boil ten potatoes (small, round ones preferred) in their skins
When done, peel them while still hot and slice in thin, round slices
Spread over the potatoes one onion, sliced fine
Sprinkle generously with salt and pepper
Add one tablespoon of mustard seed, one-half tablespoon of celery seed, and one-half tablespoon of sugar
Beat one egg until light
Pour two tablespoons of goose or chicken fat, melted, over the eggs
Stir well
Add one-half cup of vinegar
Pour over the seasoned potatoes
Add one-quarter cup of hot water and if necessary, add a little more vinegar, salt or pepper
One or two chopped hard-boiled eggs may be added to improve the salad
Line a salad bowl with lettuce leaves
Pour in the salad and decorate the top with grated hard-boiled eggs

title: Potato Salad, No. 2
description: A salad made with potatoes, onions, and vinegar.

ingredients.name: one quart of small Bermuda potatoes
ingredients.sourceText: one quart of small Bermuda potatoes

steps: Wash and scrub the potatoes thoroughly in cold water
Put them in a kettle with enough cold water, slightly salted, just to cover them
Stand them over a brisk fire with the kettle covered until the water begins to boil
Turn down the heat, lift the cover of the kettle slightly, and let the potatoes cook slowly till done
Drain off the water and stand the potatoes where they will get cold, but do not put them in a refrigerator
When quite cold, peel the potatoes and slice them very thin in a salad bowl
To every two layers of potato slices sprinkle over a very light layer of white onions sliced very thin
Pour over the salad a French dressing made of equal parts of oil and vinegar with tarragon vinegar, salt and pepper
When ready to serve, cover the surface of the salad with a stiff mayonnaise in which a suggestion of cream has been mixed
Ornament with quarters of hard-boiled eggs, boiled beets cut in fancy slices and a fringe of parsley around the edge of the bowl

title: Preserved Peaches
description: Prepared with peaches, sugar, and water.
steps: Weigh one pound of sugar for each pound of fruit
Brush each peach with a stiff whiskbroom
Peel the peaches very thin with a sharp silver knife
As fast as the peaches are peeled lay them on porcelain platters
Put the peelings in the preserving kettle with enough water to keep from sticking
Stand the kettle over rather a quick fire and let the peelings boil with the kettle covered until very soft
Then drain them through a colander and pour the juice strained back into the kettle
Add sugar to this and let it simmer gently until it is a thick syrup
During the time the syrup is cooking it must be frequently stirred and skimmed
As soon as the syrup is thick enough, drop in the peaches, twelve at a time if for quart jars, and six at a time if for pint jars
Let the peaches cook gently until each one may easily be pierced with a broom splint
Then quickly skim them out and lay them on a platter to cool
Repeat this process until all the peaches are done
Let the syrup cook until thick as molasses
Skim it thoroughly
When cool put the peaches, one at a time, in the jars with a spoon

When the syrup is sufficiently thick, pour it through a strainer over the peaches in the jars until they are full, then seal down quickly and stand them upside down for several hours before putting them in the store-room

title: Puff-Paste
description: Prepared with fat or veal or beef, oil, and flour.
steps: Let the melted fat get warm and soft like butter, put with 2 tablespoonfuls of oil, mix it well and beat it till it is white as snow and just the consistency of butter
Place in a basin 1 lb. of flour to make puff-paste, it must be the best
Take up the lb. of fat you have beaten in the lump, lay it on the flour, turn it over to cover it with flour, lay it on the paste board
Make a paste with the remainder of the flour with a little cold water, not harder or softer than the fat
Roll it out on the board, then take the lump of fat, lay it on top and roll it over the paste
Sprinkle a little flour over, then fold it up on the board and cover it with the basin you made it in, and let it be for one hour
If in summer it must be put in a very cold place for the fat not to melt; if in winter, you can leave it in the kitchen, as the fat must not get hard
Be very particular not to handle it too much, and as light as you can; before beginning it in the summer let the cold water run well over your hands
Sometimes in the summer you have to put it on ice to get it the proper firmness
After it has laid for an hour, put it on your paste board, roll it out lightly 3 times

title: Quince Jelly
description: Prepared with quinces and sugar.
steps: Prepare the fruit and cook peels and cores as directed for preserving.
Cut the quinces in small pieces and let them boil in the strained water for one hour with kettle uncovered.
When cooked the desired length of time, pour the whole into a jelly-bag of white flannel or double cheese-cloth; hang over a big bowl or jar and let the liquor all drain through.
This will take several hours.
When all the liquor is drained, measure it and return to the kettle.
To each pint of liquor weigh a pound of sugar.
While the liquor is heating put the sugar in the oven, then add to the boiling hot liquor and stir it until sugar is melted.

When the whole is thick, and drops from the spoon like jelly, pour it through a strainer into the jelly glasses; and when the jelly is cool, put on the covers — first pouring a film of melted paraffin over the surface.

title: Sauerkraut
description: Prepared with cabbage, apples, and grapes.
steps: Line the bottom and sides of a clean barrel or keg with cabbage leaves.
Cut into fine shreds one or two dozen large heads of white, crisp cabbage.
Put in a layer of cabbage, say about four inches deep, and press down firmly and sprinkle with about four tablespoons of salt.
Put one or two tart apples, cut up fine, between each layer, or some Malaga grapes.
When four layers have been put in, pound with a wooden beetle until the cabbage is quite compact.
Add more cabbage, and so on until all has been salted, always pounding down each layer.
Cover with cabbage leaves, then a clean cloth, a well-fitting board, and a heavy stone, to act as weight on top of all.
Set away in a cool cellar to ferment.
In two weeks examine, remove the scum, if any; wash the cloth, board and stone, wash also the sides of the keg or jar, and place all back again.
This must be done weekly.

Put on the tongues gracefully with some more of the egg, sausage, parsley, and beetroot
Fill the mould up

title: Sister Cake, the Queen of Cakes
description: A cake made with dough, ground almonds, and citron.
steps: Put the dough in a very nice pan, put it near the fire to warm.
Melt the 1 lb. of butter in a teacup of milk, taking a piece of the butter first to rub your dish with.
Beat up the 6 eggs, put them in the pan with the dough.
Put in the ground almonds, then the butter and milk, a small pinch of salt.
Beat it all well for 1 hour.
Have ready a nice round yellow dish, butter it well.
Cut up the citron in slices in one plate, then the orange and lemon in another.
Put at the bottom of your dish a layer of the mixture of dough, butter, almonds, etc., then a layer of citron, then dough, then orange and lemon.
Continue making layers till you have used up all your ingredients, making your layer very lightly.
Your oven must be ready for it as soon as it is made, not a fierce oven.
It will take an hour to bake and will rise very much.
Put an iron skewer through to see if it is done; if the skewer comes out clean it is done.
Have 2 oz. of Jordan almonds bleached, put them on a plate in the oven to dry and get a light brown colour.
Put the 3 lbs. of sugar in a very clean saucepan with a pint of water, let it boil till it comes like a syrup.
Throw the orange-flower water in.
Have the sugar ready when the cake is done, as it must be poured hot when the cake comes out of the oven.
Just pass a knife round to let it soak.

Turn the liquor into a small saucepan, mix a spoonful of flour with a glass of white wine, stir it into the liquor, let it boil to get thick like another sauce
